Prerequisites: 03 · Triangles, area and surface normals, 05 · Barycentric coordinates and interpolation

Nearest vertex is not nearest surface

A point-cloud neighbor search asks which stored reference points are closest to each query. A closest-point-on-mesh query instead searches triangle interiors, edges and corners. A point above the middle of a large triangle may be close to its surface and far from every vertex. Replacing surface distance with vertex distance therefore changes the optimization objective, not just its speed.

Neighbor identity is a discrete selection. Within a region where the same reference point wins, the squared-distance gradient with respect to q is 2(q-r). At a tie, that selected expression can change. A deterministic tie rule makes repeated execution reproducible; it does not make the mathematical nearest-neighbor function smooth.

Worked example

For segment a=(0,0), b=(2,0) and query q=(1,2), project onto the segment direction:

Here t=0.5, closest point p=(1,0), squared distance is four and distance is two. A query at (3,2) instead clamps to endpoint (2,0), giving squared distance five. Triangle queries similarly split into face, edge and vertex regions, rather than always using a plane projection that might fall outside the triangle.

What the loss does and does not know

An unsigned distance cannot tell inside from outside. A point on either side of a thin surface can have the same loss. A symmetric Chamfer-style objective averages nearest-point distances in both directions, but still does not encode topology, one-to-one correspondence or normals unless additional terms are added. Uneven sampling density can change how strongly regions are weighted. Outliers may dominate a squared loss.

Try it yourself

Why is a nearest-neighbor test with only one reference point insufficient?

Answer

It checks distance arithmetic but cannot reveal wrong ranking, tie handling, batch leakage or the handling of fewer valid neighbors than requested.

gffx boundary

knn reports squared distances, selected indices and validity. closest_point_on_mesh additionally reports face, barycentrics and closest coordinates, but only its squared-distance output propagates the supported cotangent. Do not silently optimize through closest-point or barycentric outputs as though their region-dependent Jacobians were implemented. No inside/outside classifier, acceleration structure or robust registration system is implied by the baseline proximity primitives.
